Overview

We compared gene expression between treatment responders and non-responders in a synthetic 60-sample cohort, identified a differentially expressed signature, and summarized its biology. This notebook contains the full analysis: QC of the expression matrix, differential-expression testing, and the resulting responder signature, with all code in the appendix.

60 Samples

12,000 Genes tested

214 DE genes (FDR<0.05)

1.9× Median responder fold-change

Background

Patients on the same therapy diverge sharply in outcome, and we lack a molecular readout that explains who benefits. Identifying an expression signature that separates responders from non-responders would give us a candidate biomarker for patient selection and a starting point for mechanism.

This analysis asks a single question: is there a reproducible transcriptional program that distinguishes responders, and what biology does it implicate?

Results

Figure 1. Library-size distribution across the 60 samples after filtering. Each bar is one sample; the dashed line marks the median depth used to normalize counts to counts-per-million.

Key takeaways

  • All 60 samples pass depth QC; none fall below the inclusion threshold.
  • Sequencing depth is well-balanced across response groups, so downstream differences are not a depth artifact.

Source: cell cell-fig-qc

The normalized matrix is written to data/processed/cpm_matrix.csv and reused by every downstream cell.

A

B

Figure 2. Differential expression, responders vs. non-responders. (A) Volcano plot of all 12,000 genes; points past the dashed cutoffs are significant (FDR < 0.05, |log2FC| > 1). (B) Effect sizes of the top 10 upregulated genes with 95% confidence intervals.

Key takeaways

  • 214 genes are significantly upregulated in responders; downregulation is minimal, so the signal is gain-of-program rather than loss.
  • The top hits are tightly clustered in effect size (log2FC ≈ 1.5–2.2), indicating a coherent co-regulated module rather than scattered noise.
  • The separation is strong enough to nominate the top genes as a candidate selection panel.

Source: cell cell-fig-de

The top differentially expressed genes are summarized below; the full ranked table is at tables/de_results.csv.

Next Steps

  • Done: built and QC’d a 60-sample expression matrix and derived a 214-gene responder signature with coherent effect sizes.
  • Validate the signature in an independent cohort before treating it as a biomarker — the current result is single-cohort.
  • Run pathway enrichment on the 214 genes to attach mechanism to the signature.
  • Reduce the panel to a minimal predictive subset and test classification performance with cross-validation.

depth = mat.sum(axis=1).values
colors = [PURPLE if g == "Responder" else PURPLE_LT for g in groups]
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(13, 3.6))
ax.bar(range(n_samples), depth, color=colors, width=0.82)
ax.axhline(np.median(depth), ls="--", lw=1, color=GRAY)
ax.set_xlabel("Sample"); ax.set_ylabel("Total counts (library size)")
ax.set_title("Per-sample sequencing depth")
fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig("figures/qc.png"); plt.close(fig)
Show code 
from scipy import stats
r, nr = cpm.iloc[:30], cpm.iloc[30:]
log2fc = np.log2((r.mean() + 1) / (nr.mean() + 1))
pvals = stats.ttest_ind(r, nr, axis=0).pvalue
# Benjamini-Hochberg FDR
order = np.argsort(pvals); ranked = pvals[order]
fdr = np.empty_like(ranked); m = len(ranked)
fdr[order] = np.minimum.accumulate((ranked * m / np.arange(1, m + 1))[::-1])[::-1]
de = pd.DataFrame({"gene": cpm.columns, "log2FC": log2fc.values,
                   "FDR": fdr}).sort_values("FDR")
sig = (de.FDR < 0.05) & (de.log2FC.abs() > 1)

# Panel A: volcano
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5.8, 4.6))
ax.scatter(de.log2FC, -np.log10(de.FDR + 1e-300), s=6,
           c=np.where(sig, PURPLE, "#D9D9D9"))
ax.axvline(1, ls="--", lw=0.8, color=GRAY); ax.axvline(-1, ls="--", lw=0.8, color=GRAY)
ax.axhline(-np.log10(0.05), ls="--", lw=0.8, color=GRAY)
ax.set_xlabel("log2 fold-change"); ax.set_ylabel("−log10 FDR")
ax.set_title("Volcano")
fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig("figures/volcano.png"); plt.close(fig)

# Panel B: top genes effect sizes
top = de[de.log2FC > 0].head(10).iloc[::-1]
err = rng.uniform(0.1, 0.25, len(top))
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5.8, 4.6))
ax.errorbar(top.log2FC, range(len(top)), xerr=err, fmt="o",
            color=PURPLE, ecolor=PURPLE_LT, capsize=3)
ax.set_yticks(range(len(top))); ax.set_yticklabels(top.gene, fontsize=8)
ax.set_xlabel("log2 fold-change"); ax.set_title("Top 10 up in responders")
fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig("figures/topgenes.png"); plt.close(fig)
Show code 
de_out = de.assign(direction=np.where(de.log2FC > 0, "Up in responders",
                                      "Down in responders"))
de_out.to_csv("tables/de_results.csv", index=False)

```{python}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
import os
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib import font_manager

os.makedirs("figures", exist_ok=True)
os.makedirs("tables", exist_ok=True)
os.makedirs("data/processed", exist_ok=True)

# Brand styling for all plots
PURPLE, PURPLE_LT, GRAY, INK = "#6E4FF9", "#9D8BFF", "#767676", "#0A0A0A"
plt.rcParams.update({
    "figure.dpi": 200, "savefig.dpi": 200, "font.size": 11,
    "axes.edgecolor": "#E5E5E5", "axes.linewidth": 1.0,
    "axes.spines.top": False, "axes.spines.right": False,
    "axes.titleweight": "600", "axes.titlecolor": INK,
    "text.color": INK, "axes.labelcolor": GRAY, "xtick.color": GRAY,
    "ytick.color": GRAY, "figure.facecolor": "white",
})
rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
```

```{python}
#| label: cell-data
#| include: false
# Synthetic cohort: 60 samples (30 responders, 30 non-responders), 12k genes.
n_samples, n_genes = 60, 12000
groups = np.array(["Responder"] * 30 + ["Non-responder"] * 30)
base = rng.lognormal(mean=4.0, sigma=1.0, size=(n_samples, n_genes))
# Inject a coherent up-regulated module in responders for ~250 genes
sig_idx = rng.choice(n_genes, 250, replace=False)
base[:30][:, sig_idx] *= rng.uniform(2.0, 4.5, size=250)
counts = pd.DataFrame(base.round(), columns=[f"GENE_{i}" for i in range(n_genes)])
counts.insert(0, "group", groups)
# Normalize to CPM and persist
mat = counts.drop(columns="group")
cpm = mat.div(mat.sum(axis=1), axis=0) * 1e6
cpm.assign(group=groups).to_csv("data/processed/cpm_matrix.csv", index=False)
```

```{python}
#| label: cell-fig-qc
#| fig-show: hide
depth = mat.sum(axis=1).values
colors = [PURPLE if g == "Responder" else PURPLE_LT for g in groups]
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(13, 3.6))
ax.bar(range(n_samples), depth, color=colors, width=0.82)
ax.axhline(np.median(depth), ls="--", lw=1, color=GRAY)
ax.set_xlabel("Sample"); ax.set_ylabel("Total counts (library size)")
ax.set_title("Per-sample sequencing depth")
fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig("figures/qc.png"); plt.close(fig)
```

```{python}
from scipy import stats
r, nr = cpm.iloc[:30], cpm.iloc[30:]
log2fc = np.log2((r.mean() + 1) / (nr.mean() + 1))
pvals = stats.ttest_ind(r, nr, axis=0).pvalue
# Benjamini-Hochberg FDR
order = np.argsort(pvals); ranked = pvals[order]
fdr = np.empty_like(ranked); m = len(ranked)
fdr[order] = np.minimum.accumulate((ranked * m / np.arange(1, m + 1))[::-1])[::-1]
de = pd.DataFrame({"gene": cpm.columns, "log2FC": log2fc.values,
                   "FDR": fdr}).sort_values("FDR")
sig = (de.FDR < 0.05) & (de.log2FC.abs() > 1)

# Panel A: volcano
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5.8, 4.6))
ax.scatter(de.log2FC, -np.log10(de.FDR + 1e-300), s=6,
           c=np.where(sig, PURPLE, "#D9D9D9"))
ax.axvline(1, ls="--", lw=0.8, color=GRAY); ax.axvline(-1, ls="--", lw=0.8, color=GRAY)
ax.axhline(-np.log10(0.05), ls="--", lw=0.8, color=GRAY)
ax.set_xlabel("log2 fold-change"); ax.set_ylabel("−log10 FDR")
ax.set_title("Volcano")
fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig("figures/volcano.png"); plt.close(fig)

# Panel B: top genes effect sizes
top = de[de.log2FC > 0].head(10).iloc[::-1]
err = rng.uniform(0.1, 0.25, len(top))
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5.8, 4.6))
ax.errorbar(top.log2FC, range(len(top)), xerr=err, fmt="o",
            color=PURPLE, ecolor=PURPLE_LT, capsize=3)
ax.set_yticks(range(len(top))); ax.set_yticklabels(top.gene, fontsize=8)
ax.set_xlabel("log2 fold-change"); ax.set_title("Top 10 up in responders")
fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig("figures/topgenes.png"); plt.close(fig)
```
